turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come in, sit down. What has been happening?

[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Doctor, I am having this wheezing, it came after a cold. Actually my internal exams were last week, I sat in the library till late, and the bus home was packed, so maybe I caught it there.

[SEG0003] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Doctor, I am his mother, I stay with him and I look after the medicines. This wheezing is going on for ten days. Yesterday he was warm, I think fever was there, and he did not sleep the whole night.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Amma, no. The cold was longer, but the wheeze is only from four days. I didn't have fever, I was just sweating with the breathing. I slept, I woke one time only.

[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me say that back: the cold came first, you say the wheeze is four days and your mother says about ten days, and she felt you were feverish while you say there was no fever. I'll note both versions. How did the cold start?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Runny nose and a sore throat. Now the nose is okay, throat also settled. Then the chest became tight, that whistling feeling.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Is the cough bringing up any phlegm?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Dry cough only, worse in the night. No phlegm, nothing yellow or green.
[SEG0009] person_3 (CAREGIVER): From his room I could hear the whistle. He was very restless, doctor.
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): The whistle is the wheeze, that part is true. But I was not sitting up the whole night, I sat once, took the pump, and lay down again.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): One waking, then. When you walk, are you short of breath?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): On the stairs, yes, and if I talk a lot. Just sitting, I am okay. I had to skip cricket practice, and we have a match on Sunday, which is really bothering me.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain along with this?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): No chest pain.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Which inhaler are you using, and how many times?

[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): The brown one, I think that is for the attack, and I have been taking it maybe five, six times a day. Or wait, is the blue the one? I always mix those two up. The chemist just says use the pump, he doesn't explain.
[SEG0017] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Blue one stays in his pocket, brown one is on the table. When the cough comes he grabs the blue. Brown was meant for morning and night, but he forgets the night.

[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Sorry, yes, mostly the blue, two puffs, maybe five, six times in the day. Brown I take in the morning, one puff, and the evening I miss often. The blue helps for some time, then the tightness comes back.

[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'll separate them clearly: blue is salbutamol, your reliever for when you are wheezy, and brown is the preventer, a steroid inhaler for every day, not only for attacks. Five or six times with the blue is more than we want. What strength is written on the blue one?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): Hundred micrograms, salbutamol, it is printed on the canister. I looked while we were in the auto, just to be sure.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): And the brown inhaler, the name on the box?
[SEG0022] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Beclomethasone, 200 micrograms. The old plan was morning and night. He takes one puff in the morning and skips the night, I have seen it.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): That is right, one puff in the morning. Night-time I miss it, not always, but often. I won't pretend otherwise.
[SEG0024] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any other tablets recently? And any allergy to a medicine?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No tablets. I did steam and some ginger tea, my neighbour swears ginger cures all this, I am not so sure. No allergy to any medicine.
[SEG0026] person_3 (CAREGIVER): Asthma is there from class six. His father also used to get this same wheezing.

[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, asthma from school days. Last year, at the college health check, they did spirometry, that blowing test, and they said it was borderline. No proper number, just borderline.
[SEG0028] person_1 (DOCTOR): Known asthma, then, and a spirometry last year reported as borderline, without a figure. Do you smoke?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked. I stay with my mother, second year commerce. I don't drink either, except one sip at a cousin's wedding, and that was horrible, so never again.
[SEG0030] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright. I'll listen to your chest now, just breathe normally through your mouth.

[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): There is a wheeze on both sides, when you breathe out. No crackles. The nurse did your peak flow outside, three tries, 290, 320 and 340. Best is 340 litres per minute, and that is low.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): 340, okay, that sounds poor. I was also thinking about the college fest banners, but that can wait. Is this serious, doctor?

[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): My working impression is an asthma flare after that viral cold. I am not calling it a new diagnosis, you already have asthma. I want to add a short course of steroid tablets.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Tablets? I won't get a swollen face, no? I have a presentation on Thursday, I have to look normal. Kindly say how many days.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): Prednisolone, 40 mg, once a day, for five days. Take it after breakfast. A course this short will not change your face. It is to settle the wheeze.
[SEG0036] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will put it next to his breakfast, otherwise he forgets. What about the two pumps?

[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Blue salbutamol, two puffs when you are wheezy. If you still need it more than every four hours, come back sooner, don't sit on it. Brown beclomethasone, one puff in the morning and one puff at night, every single day, including good days.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Night puff also, every day, and the blue not five-six times. Should I do a blood test, or an x-ray? My uncle did an x-ray for his cough and it was a whole drama.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): No blood test and no x-ray today, I don't think they will change anything. I want to see you in one week. If your breathing gets worse, or you cannot finish a sentence, go to emergency the same day.
[SEG0040] person_3 (CAREGIVER): If he vomits the tablet, do I give another?

[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): If he vomits within about half an hour, repeat that one dose. If it is later than that, leave it, and mention it when I see him. Blue is for relief, brown is for prevention, keep that straight.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): Blue relief, brown prevention. I'll park the brown next to my toothbrush. My cousin stores his inhaler in the fridge, which is mad, no?

[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): Room temperature is fine, not the fridge. Let me pull it together: wheeze somewhere between four and ten days after a cold, you deny fever while your mother thought you were warm, dry cough, breathless on stairs, blue salbutamol two puffs maybe five or six times a day, and brown beclomethasone one puff in the morning with the night dose often missed. On examination there is wheeze on both sides and the best peak flow is 340. Plan is prednisolone 40 mg after breakfast for five days, the inhalers as we discussed, and a review in one week, sooner if you worsen.
[SEG0044] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I will watch the tablets and the night pump. We will be here in one week.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Thank you. Maybe I can at least field on Sunday, we'll see. Do I start the tablet today or from tomorrow?
[SEG0046] person_1 (DOCTOR): Start today, after food. If you have already eaten, you can take the 40 mg when you get home. Otherwise eat first. I will see you in a week.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): We had idli in the morning, so food is done. I'll take it at home. The pharmacy queue is always long, that is the only problem.
[SEG0048] person_3 (CAREGIVER): I have his old inhaler slip in my bag, if they ask for it. We will manage the new tablets.
[SEG0049] person_1 (DOCTOR): They will take today's prescription for the prednisolone. Go carefully, and don't wait if the breathing turns.
